target_customer: Indian college students who pay a share of salary after getting a tech job (income share agreement); revenue comes from graduates and hiring partners
problem: Few Indian college graduates have the algorithm and interview skills for top tech jobs, and good teachers are scarce; AlgoUniversity uses live cohorts led by a small group of expert educators.
business_model: Income share agreement: year long live cohort training paid as a portion of salary after placement
product_category: Online tech education and ISA based bootcamp

founders.name: Manas Kumar Verma
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page without a bio. Other aggregators call him CEO and co-founder.

founders.name: Swapnil Daga
founders.background_notes: YC page says he was lead instructor at other edtech startups for over two years and now scales the teaching infrastructure. University not named.

technical_complexity.rationale: Live teaching infrastructure and cohort tooling on top of standard video and learning platforms; the difficulty is operational, not technical.

defensibility.rationale: Placement outcomes and educator access matter, but the model is imitable by other Indian bootcamps.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying AlgoUniversity.

market_need_then: India produces many engineering graduates with limited access to strong tech training; the YC page states the premise but I found no dated spend or placement data.

branding.community_and_virality: A Product Hunt page exists and G2 shows 10 reviews; no merch or community found

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that signals algorithms education, but little press about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: AlgoUniversity is listed Active with about 40 people in Hyderabad, running year long live cohorts under an income share model. Public funding information is thin and unverified, and no news on layoffs, sale or shutdown was found. The ISA model defers revenue until graduates are placed, which strains cash, but outcome details are not public.
notes: Unverified funding: CB Insights alone lists about 130K USD over three rounds with a seed on 2021-09 from Y Combinator, Zentani and Soma Capital; Persana says undisclosed. Not recorded as a round. Founding year conflicts (CB Insights says 2020); YC page value not captured, so founded_year is null. Company site (algouniversity.com) was fetched: it says the company was founded by IIIT Hyderabad alumni, lists Manas Kumar Verma as CEO and Swapnil Daga as co-founder and COO, gives no funding or competitors, and says outcomes were built since 2020. Competitors (Scaler, Newton School, Masai) appear only on 2026 comparison pages, no dated source near 2021, so the list is empty. TheOrg says it was founded by IIIT Hyderabad alumni, single aggregator, not used for education. Outcome search found nothing about this company.
